title: Non-Hermitian Holographic Flows to Little Rip Cosmologies
authors: Daniel Arean, David Garcia-Fariña, Juan F. Pedraza
abstract: Spacelike singularities supported by matter satisfying the null energy condition (NEC) are expected to fall within the Belinski--Khalatnikov--Lifshitz (BKL) paradigm. We show that controlled violations of the NEC in holography can lead to different black hole interiors. In a holographic model dual to a strongly coupled non-Hermitian $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric QFT, we uncover a novel non-Kasner regime within its real, $\mathcal{PT}$-restored phase. The deep-interior geometry describes an isotropic FLRW cosmology undergoing super-accelerated expansion and approaching a Little Rip. This regime leaves a characteristic imprint on two-sided heavy-operator correlators, allowing it to be distinguished from a standard Kasner interior. Our construction provides a concrete holographic realization of a Little Rip cosmology and lays the groundwork for a Little Rip/CFT correspondence, in which such cosmological regimes can be explored through observables in a non-Hermitian quantum field theory.
summary: This paper develops a holographic framework to model cosmological singularities beyond the standard BKL description. By introducing controlled violations of the Null Energy Condition through non-Hermitian quantum field theories, the authors predict the existence of a Little Rip cosmology in black hole interiors. This work establishes a potential 'Little Rip/CFT correspondence' using advanced diagnostic tools like heavy-operator correlators.
main_problem: The research aims to understand cosmological singularities beyond the standard BKL paradigm by analyzing holographic flows derived from non-Hermitian quantum field theories.
main_result: Controlled violations of the Null Energy Condition via non-Hermiticity lead to a novel, isotropic Little Rip cosmology in the black hole interior, distinct from standard Kasner behavior.
method: The study employs holographic techniques (AdS/CFT) to map bulk geometry dynamics onto boundary QFT observables, utilizing analysis of two-sided heavy-operator correlators and thermal state properties.
model_or_system: The model is a holographic dual to a strongly coupled non-Hermitian PT-symmetric QFT. The system involves analyzing the evolution of black hole interiors under conditions violating the NEC.
key_observables: Two-sided heavy-operator correlators, geodesic length $L_{	ext{ren}}(E)$, and the equation of state $p = -\epsilon - 2\alpha$.
important_parameters: The ratio $\eta = |s_{nh}/s_h|$ governing the balance between non-Hermitian ($s_{nh}$) and Hermitian ($s_h$) sources, and the asymptotic behavior of energy density ($\epsilon \propto \log a$).
main_assumptions: The connection between the deep interior geometry (bulk) and boundary observables (correlators) via the holographic dictionary is central; approximations are used for near-horizon expansion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate energy level spectra in PT-symmetric regimes, compare numerical vs. analytical field values ($	ilde{g}, 	ilde{f}, \psi, R$) across vast scales, and show diagnostic plots related to geodesic length decay rates.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework connecting non-Hermiticity to NEC violation (Chunk 1), then analyzing this using toy models of thermal states and PT symmetry restoration (Chunk 2), culminating in a detailed geometric analysis comparing Little Rip scaling against Kasner metrics (Chunk 3).
why_interesting: The explicit connection between open quantum systems physics (PT-symmetry, non-Hermiticity) and fundamental gravitational/cosmological endpoints (Little Rip) provides a powerful theoretical tool for studying extreme spacetime regimes.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Energy levels in the two-level system (1.2). For |Γ/g| > 1 the energies become complex conjugate and PT symmetry is broken.

Figure 2: Free energy of solutions with v = 1 and T/M = 0.5 (left) and T/M = 1 (right) as a function of η. For |η| > 1 two branches of solutions exist. The green branch has lower free energy and is thus thermodynamically preferred. The two branches meet at |ηc| ≈1.49 (left) and |ηc| ≈2.43 (right). For |η| > |ηc| only complex geometries exist: the red dashed line shows the real part of their free energy. In the insets we plot the free energy of the green branch in a log-log plot: it approaches a constant as |η| →1+.

Figure 3: Kasner coefficients for the non-Hermitian model with v = 1 at T/M = 0.5 in the PT -symmetric phase (|η| < 1) and in the subdominant branch of the PT - restored phase (1 < |η| < ηc ≈1.49). The Kasner coefficients are continuous and diverge as |η| →ηs ≈1.47. For ηs < |η| < ηc the subdominant branch of the PT -restored phase does not have a Kasner singularity and instead has the same singularity as in the dominant branch. In the plot, the red dashed line corresponds to ηc and the black dashed line to ηs.

Figure 4: Fields and Ricci scalar in the dominant branch of the PT -restored phase for a solution with v = 1, T/M = 0.5 and η = 1.45. The blue line represents the patch with coordinate z while the red line denotes the patch with coordinate ˜z. As ˜z →0, g goes to a constant but f and ψ diverge. We conclude that ˜z →0 is a singularity as R diverges as we approach that point.

Figure 5: Kasner coefficients for the non-Hermitian model with v = 1 at T/M = 0.5 in the PT -broken phase. The solid lines denote the real part of the Kasner coefficients and the dashed line the imaginary part. In this phase the geometry is complex and so are the Kasner coefficients.
